questions.text: किसी पतली प्लास्टिक की छड़ को त्रिज्या R के वृत्ताकार वलय के रूप में मोड़ा गया है। इसे आवेश घनत्व λ से एकसमान आवेशित किया गया है। इसके केन्द्र पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र का परिमाण है :
questions.text_english: A thin plastic rod is bent into a circular ring of radius R. It is uniformly charged with charge density λ. The magnitude of the electric field at its centre is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Zero. A uniformly charged circular ring has charge distributed symmetrically about its centre. For every small charge element on one side of the ring, there is an equal and opposite charge element diametrically opposite. The electric field contributions from these pairs cancel out completely by symmetry. Therefore, the net electric field at the centre of a uniformly charged circular ring is always zero. Options A, C, and D give non-zero values, which are incorrect as they do not account for the complete cancellation due to circular symmetry.
questions.topic: Electric field due to a ring of charge

questions.text: तीन आवेशित छोटे गोले X, Y और Z जिन पर क्रमश: आवेश +q, –q और +q हैं, आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार एक-दूसरे से समदूरस्थ स्थित हैं। गोले Y और Z को स्थिर रखा गया है। आरम्भ में X भी अपने स्थान पर स्थिर है परन्तु यह गति के लिए स्वतंत्र है। जब X को मुक्त किया जाता है, तो इसके द्वारा चला गया पथ होगा :
questions.text_english: Three small charged spheres X, Y and Z carrying charges +q, –q and +q respectively are placed equidistant from each other, as shown in the figure. The spheres Y and Z are held in place. Initially X is also held in place, but is otherwise free to move. When X is released, the path followed by it will be :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) path C. Sphere X carries charge +q. It is attracted towards Y (which has charge –q) and repelled by Z (which has charge +q). The net force on X is the vector sum of the attractive force toward Y and the repulsive force away from Z. Since Y and Z are equidistant and the geometry is symmetric, the resultant force on X points toward the right and slightly curved, following path C. Paths A, B and D do not correctly represent the direction of the net electrostatic force on X.
questions.topic: Coulomb's law and superposition of forces

questions.text: किसी एकसमान सीधे तार में, चालन इलेक्ट्रॉन +x दिशा के अनुदिश गमन करते हैं। मान लीजिए तार में E और j क्रमश: विद्युत-क्षेत्र और धारा घनत्व हैं। तब :
questions.text_english: In a uniform straight wire, conduction electrons move along +x direction. Let E and j be the electric field and current density in the wire, respectively. Then :

options.A: E और j दोनों +x दिशा के अनुदिश हैं।
options.B: E और j दोनों –x दिशा के अनुदिश हैं।
options.C: E +x दिशा के अनुदिश, परन्तु j –x दिशा के अनुदिश है।
options.D: E –x दिशा के अनुदिश, परन्तु j +x दिशा के अनुदिश है।

options_english.A: E and j both are along +x direction.
options_english.B: E and j both are along –x direction.
options_english.C: E is along +x direction, but j is along –x direction.
options_english.D: E is along –x direction, but j is along +x direction.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Electrons move in the +x direction, meaning conventional current flows in the –x direction. Wait — conventional current flows opposite to electron flow, so if electrons move in +x direction, conventional current flows in –x direction. However, the electric field E drives conventional current in its own direction, so E is along –x direction. Current density j follows conventional current, so j is also along –x direction. Therefore option (B) is correct: both E and j are along –x direction. The electrons move opposite to E because they are negatively charged. Option A is incorrect. The correct answer is (B).
questions.topic: Current density and electric field in conductors

questions.text: दो आवेशित कणों P और Q जिन पर समान आवेश q परन्तु जिनके द्रव्यमान m₁ और m₂ हैं, को समान विभवान्तर V द्वारा त्वरित किया गया है। ये चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B (⊥ v) के प्रदेश में प्रवेश करने पर क्रमश: a और b त्रिज्याओं के वृत्ताकार पथ पर गति करते हैं। तब (m₁/m₂) बराबर है :
questions.text_english: Two charged particles, P and Q, each having charge q but of masses m₁ and m₂, are accelerated through the same potential difference V. They enter a region of magnetic field B (⊥ v) and describe the circular paths of radii a and b respectively. Then (m₁/m₂) is equal to :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) (a/b)². When a charged particle of charge q and mass m is accelerated through potential difference V, its kinetic energy is qV = ½mv², giving v = √(2qV/m). In a magnetic field B, the radius of the circular path is r = mv/(qB) = (1/qB)√(2mqV). Therefore r ∝ √m. For particles P and Q: a/b = √(m₁/m₂), which gives m₁/m₂ = (a/b)². Options A, B, and D do not correctly follow from this derivation.
questions.topic: Circular motion of charged particles in magnetic field

questions.text: प्रतिरोध G के किसी गैल्वेनोमीटर को 0 से I A परिसर के ऐमीटर में परिवर्तित किया गया है। यदि इस गैल्वेनोमीटर में प्रवाहित धारा I A की 0.1% है, तो ऐमीटर का प्रतिरोध है :
questions.text_english: A galvanometer of resistance G is converted into an ammeter of range 0 to I A. If the current through the galvanometer is 0.1% of I A, the resistance of the ammeter is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) G/999. The galvanometer carries 0.1% of I, i.e., Ig = 0.001I. The shunt current Is = I – Ig = 0.999I. Since the galvanometer and shunt are in parallel: Ig × G = Is × S, so 0.001I × G = 0.999I × S, giving S = G/999. The ammeter resistance = S × G / (S + G) = (G/999 × G) / (G/999 + G) = G/1000. However, the question asks for the shunt resistance S = G/999. The ammeter resistance (parallel combination) is approximately G/1000, but the shunt S = G/999. The correct answer is (A) G/999.

questions.text: कोई 10 cm लम्बा तार y-अक्ष के अनुदिश रखा है। इससे धनात्मक y-दिशा में 1.0 A की धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है। इस क्षेत्र में कोई चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B = (5 mT) ĵ – (8 mT) k̂ विद्यमान है। इस तार पर बल है :
questions.text_english: A 10 cm long wire lies along y-axis. It carries a current of 1.0 A in positive y-direction. A magnetic field B = (5 mT) ĵ – (8 mT) k̂ exists in the region. The force on the wire is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) (0.8 mN) î. The force on a current-carrying wire is F = IL × B. Here L = 0.10 m ĵ, I = 1.0 A, and B = (5 mT) ĵ – (8 mT) k̂. So F = 1.0 × (0.10 ĵ) × [(5×10⁻³ ĵ) – (8×10⁻³ k̂)]. Now ĵ × ĵ = 0 and ĵ × k̂ = î. Therefore F = 1.0 × 0.10 × [0 – 8×10⁻³ î] = –8×10⁻⁴ N × (–1) = +8×10⁻⁴ N î = 0.8 mN î. The force is (0.8 mN) î.
questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field

questions.text: किसी ट्रान्सफॉर्मर की प्राथमिक और द्वितीयक कुण्डलियों में फेरों की संख्या क्रमश: 500 और 5000 है। प्राथमिक कुण्डली 220 V 50 Hz के ac स्रोत से संयोजित है। द्वितीयक कुण्डली के सिरों पर निर्गत है :
questions.text_english: The primary and secondary coils of a transformer have 500 turns and 5000 turns respectively. The primary coil is connected to an ac source of 220 V 50 Hz. The output across the secondary coil is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 2200 V 50 Hz. For a transformer, the ratio of secondary to primary voltage equals the ratio of turns: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. Here Ns/Np = 5000/500 = 10. Therefore Vs = 10 × 220 = 2200 V. The frequency of the output is always the same as the input frequency, which is 50 Hz. A transformer changes voltage but not frequency. Option C is incorrect because it shows a changed frequency of 5 Hz, which is physically impossible.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से उस वैज्ञानिक को पहचानिए, जिन्होंने सर्वप्रथम 25 mm – 5 mm परिसर की तरंगदैर्घ्यों की विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंगों को उत्पन्न करके उनका प्रेक्षण किया था :
questions.text_english: The first scientist who produced and observed electromagnetic waves of wavelengths in the range 25 mm – 5 mm was :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) J.C. Bose. Jagadish Chandra Bose was the first scientist to produce and observe electromagnetic waves in the millimetre wavelength range of 5 mm to 25 mm (microwave region). Maxwell predicted electromagnetic waves theoretically; Hertz first experimentally demonstrated radio waves of much larger wavelength; Marconi developed radio communication. Bose's pioneering work in the microwave range was ahead of its time and significantly contributed to wireless communication technology.

questions.text: किसी गतिमान इलेक्ट्रॉन और किसी गतिमान प्रोटॉन से सम्बद्ध तरंगों का तरंगदैर्घ्य समान λ है। इसका यह अभिप्राय है कि इनका/इनकी समान है :
questions.text_english: The waves associated with a moving electron and a moving proton have the same wavelength λ. It implies that they have the same :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) momentum. According to de Broglie's relation, the wavelength of a matter wave is given by λ = h/p, where h is Planck's constant and p is the momentum of the particle. If both the electron and proton have the same de Broglie wavelength λ, then they must have the same momentum p = h/λ. Their speeds, energies and angular momenta need not be equal since the electron and proton have very different masses.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: दो पुंज, A और B जिनके फ़ोटॉनों की ऊर्जा क्रमश: 3.3 eV और 11.3 eV हैं, क्रमवार किसी धात्विक पृष्ठ (कार्य-फलन 2.3 eV) को प्रदीप्त करते हैं। पुंज A के कारण उत्सर्जित इलेक्ट्रॉन की अधिकतम चाल का पुंज B से अनुपात है :
questions.text_english: Two beams, A and B whose photon energies are 3.3 eV and 11.3 eV respectively, illuminate a metallic surface (work function 2.3 eV) successively. The ratio of maximum speed of electrons emitted due to beam A to that due to beam B is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 1/3. By Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is KE = hν – φ. For beam A: KEA = 3.3 – 2.3 = 1.0 eV. For beam B: KEB = 11.3 – 2.3 = 9.0 eV. Since KE = ½mv², the speed v ∝ √(KE). Therefore vA/vB = √(KEA/KEB) = √(1/9) = 1/3. The ratio of maximum speeds is 1/3.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के स्पेक्ट्रम में बामर श्रेणी की दूसरी स्पेक्ट्रमी रेखा के निर्माण से संगत इलेक्ट्रॉन संक्रमण है :
questions.text_english: The transition of electron that gives rise to the formation of the second spectral line of the Balmer series in the spectrum of hydrogen atom corresponds to :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) nf = 2 and ni = 4. The Balmer series corresponds to transitions where the final state is n = 2. The first line of the Balmer series corresponds to ni = 3 → nf = 2 (Hα line). The second spectral line corresponds to the next transition, which is ni = 4 → nf = 2 (Hβ line). Therefore, the second Balmer line corresponds to nf = 2 and ni = 4. Option A gives the first line, and options B and D are incorrect.

questions.text: Ge का मादन As के साथ किया गया है। इसके कारण :
questions.text_english: Ge is doped with As. Due to doping,

options.A: Ge के जालक की संरचना विकृत हो जाती है।
options.B: चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या में वृद्धि होती है।
options.C: होलों की संख्या में वृद्धि होती है।
options.D: चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या में कमी होती है।

options_english.A: the structure of Ge lattice is distorted.
options_english.B: the number of conduction electrons increases.
options_english.D: the number of conduction electrons decreases.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) the number of conduction electrons increases. Arsenic (As) belongs to Group 15 and has five valence electrons, one more than germanium (Group 14). When As is used as a dopant in Ge, four of its valence electrons form covalent bonds with the four neighbouring Ge atoms, while the fifth electron becomes a free conduction electron. This process creates an n-type semiconductor where the number of conduction electrons increases significantly. The lattice structure is not significantly distorted, and holes do not increase.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : किसी बैटरी से श्रेणी में संयोजित और स्वतंत्रतापूर्वक निलम्बित दो लम्बे समान्तर तार एक-दूसरे से दूर हटते हैं।
कारण (R) : विपरीत दिशाओं में प्रवाहित धारावाही दो तार एक-दूसरे को प्रतिकर्षित करते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Two long parallel wires, freely suspended and connected in series to a battery, move apart.
Reason (R) : Two wires carrying current in opposite directions repel each other.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) प्रकार के प्रश्न। नीचे दिए गए कोडों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Assertion (A) and Reason (R) type question. Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है तथा कारण (R) भी ग़लत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). When two wires are connected in series to a battery, the current through both wires flows in the same loop. Since the wires are parallel and suspended freely, the current in one wire flows in one direction and in the return wire in the opposite direction. Two parallel wires carrying currents in opposite directions exert a repulsive force on each other. Hence, the wires move apart. Both the assertion and the reason are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : समतल दर्पण और उत्तल दर्पण किसी भी परिस्थिति में वास्तविक प्रतिबिम्ब नहीं बना सकते हैं।
कारण (R) : कोई आभासी प्रतिबिम्ब वास्तविक प्रतिबिम्ब बनाने के लिए बिम्ब की भाँति कार्य नहीं कर सकता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Plane and convex mirrors cannot produce real images under any circumstance.
Reason (R) : A virtual image cannot serve as an object to produce a real image.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) प्रकार का प्रश्न।

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है तथा कारण (R) भी ग़लत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The Assertion (A) is true — plane and convex mirrors always produce virtual, erect and diminished (or same-size for plane mirror) images and cannot form real images under normal circumstances. However, the Reason (R) is false — a virtual image can indeed serve as a virtual object for another optical element and can lead to the formation of a real image. For example, if converging rays are incident on a plane mirror, the mirror can produce a real image. Therefore Assertion is true but Reason is false.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : जब दो कुण्डलियों को एक-दूसरे के ऊपर लपेटा जाता है, तो उनके बीच अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व अधिकतम होता है।
कारण (R) : जब दो कुण्डलियाँ एक-दूसरे के ऊपर लपेटी जाती हैं तो उनके बीच फ्लक्स-संबद्धता अधिकतम होती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : The mutual inductance between two coils is maximum when the coils are wound on each other.
Reason (R) : The flux linkage between two coils is maximum when they are wound on each other.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) प्रकार का प्रश्न।

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है तथा कारण (R) भी ग़लत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Mutual inductance M = NΦ/I depends on the flux linkage NΦ between the coils. When two coils are wound on each other (bifilar winding), the entire magnetic flux produced by one coil passes through the other coil, making the flux linkage maximum. This maximum flux linkage results in maximum mutual inductance. Hence, the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : प्रकाश-विद्युत प्रभाव में, उत्सर्जित फ़ोटो-इलेक्ट्रॉनों की गतिज ऊर्जा में आपतित प्रकाश की तीव्रता में वृद्धि के साथ वृद्धि होती है।
कारण (R) : प्रकाश-विद्युत धारा आपतित प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्घ्य पर निर्भर करती है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : In photoelectric effect, the kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons increases with increase in the intensity of the incident light.
Reason (R) : Photoelectric current depends on the wavelength of the incident light.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) प्रकार का प्रश्न।

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है तथा कारण (R) भी ग़लत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). The Assertion (A) is false — according to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is KE = hν – φ, which depends only on the frequency of light, not its intensity. Increasing intensity increases the number of emitted photoelectrons (i.e., photoelectric current) but does not change their kinetic energy. The Reason (R) is also false — photoelectric current depends on the intensity of incident light, not on its wavelength. Therefore both A and R are false.

questions.text: लम्बाई L और अनुप्रस्थ-काट क्षेत्रफल A के किसी एकसमान तार का प्रतिरोध R है। इस तार को एकसमान रूप से खींचकर इसकी लम्बाई में 25% वृद्धि की गई है। तार के प्रतिरोध में प्रतिशत वृद्धि परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A uniform wire of length L and area of cross-section A has resistance R. The wire is uniformly stretched so that its length increases by 25%. Calculate the percentage increase in the resistance of the wire.

key_points: New length L' = 1.25L; volume remains constant so new area A' = A/1.25 = 4A/5
New resistance R' = ρL'/A' = ρ(1.25L)/(A/1.25) = 1.5625 ρL/A = 1.5625R
Percentage increase = (R' – R)/R × 100 = 56.25%

questions.solution: The resistance of the wire is R = ρL/A. When the wire is stretched by 25%, its new length becomes L' = 1.25L. Since the volume of the wire remains constant, L × A = L' × A', giving A' = LA/L' = A/1.25 = 0.8A. The new resistance is R' = ρL'/A' = ρ × 1.25L / 0.8A = 1.5625 × (ρL/A) = 1.5625R. Therefore, the percentage increase in resistance = (R' – R)/R × 100 = (1.5625R – R)/R × 100 = 0.5625 × 100 = 56.25%.

questions.text: कोई बिम्ब 40 cm वक्रता त्रिज्या के किसी अवतल दर्पण के सामने 30 cm दूरी पर स्थित है। (i) बने प्रतिबिम्ब की स्थिति तथा (ii) प्रतिबिम्ब का आवर्धन ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature 40 cm. Find the (i) position of the image formed and (ii) magnification of the image.

key_points: Focal length f = –R/2 = –20 cm; object distance u = –30 cm
Using mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f → 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = –1/20 + 1/30 = –1/60; v = –60 cm
Magnification m = –v/u = –(–60)/(–30) = –2 (real, inverted, magnified image)

questions.solution: For the concave mirror, the focal length f = –R/2 = –40/2 = –20 cm. The object is at u = –30 cm. Using the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f: 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = 1/(–20) – 1/(–30) = –1/20 + 1/30 = (–3 + 2)/60 = –1/60. Therefore v = –60 cm. The image is formed 60 cm in front of the mirror on the same side as the object, meaning it is a real image. The magnification m = –v/u = –(–60)/(–30) = –2. The image is real, inverted, and twice the size of the object.

questions.text: गतिज ऊर्जा E के किसी न्यूट्रॉन (द्रव्यमान m) तथा समान ऊर्जा के किसी फ़ोटॉन पर विचार कीजिए। मान लीजिए न्यूट्रॉन की दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य λn तथा फ़ोटॉन की तरंगदैर्घ्य λp है। λn/λp के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Consider a neutron (mass m) of kinetic energy E and a photon of the same energy. Let λn and λp be the de Broglie wavelength of neutron and the wavelength of photon respectively. Obtain an expression for λn/λp.

key_points: For neutron: KE = p²/2m → p = √(2mE); λn = h/p = h/√(2mE)
For photon: E = hc/λp → λp = hc/E
λn/λp = [h/√(2mE)] / [hc/E] = E/(c√(2mE)) = √(E/2mc²)

questions.solution: For the neutron of kinetic energy E and mass m, the momentum is p = √(2mE). Using de Broglie's relation, λn = h/p = h/√(2mE). For the photon with the same energy E, using E = hc/λp, we get λp = hc/E. Therefore, the ratio λn/λp = [h/√(2mE)] ÷ [hc/E] = h × E / [c × h × √(2mE)] = E / [c√(2mE)] = √(E) / [c√(2m)] = √(E / 2mc²). Hence λn/λp = √(E/2mc²).

questions.text: (क) आवृत्ति 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz का एकवर्णी प्रकाश वायु से अपवर्तनांक 1.5 वाले माध्यम में गमन करता है। दोनों माध्यमों के अन्तरापृष्ठ पर (i) परावर्तित प्रकाश, तथा (ii) अपवर्तित प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्घ्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Monochromatic light of frequency 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz passes from air into a medium of refractive index 1.5. Find the wavelength of the light (i) reflected, and (ii) refracted at the interface of the two media.

sub_questions.text: (क) आवृत्ति 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz का एकवर्णी प्रकाश वायु से अपवर्तनांक 1.5 वाले माध्यम में गमन करता है। दोनों माध्यमों के अन्तरापृष्ठ पर (i) परावर्तित प्रकाश, तथा (ii) अपवर्तित प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्घ्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Monochromatic light of frequency 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz passes from air into a medium of refractive index 1.5. Find the wavelength of the light (i) reflected, and (ii) refracted at the interface of the two media.

key_points: Reflected light remains in air: λ_reflected = c/ν = 3×10⁸ / 5×10¹⁴ = 6×10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm
Refracted light in medium: λ_refracted = λ_air / n = 600 nm / 1.5 = 400 nm

sub_questions.solution: The wavelength of reflected light remains the same as in air since reflection does not change the medium. λ_reflected = c/ν = (3 × 10⁸) / (5.0 × 10¹⁴) = 6 × 10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm. When light enters the medium of refractive index n = 1.5, its frequency stays the same but wavelength changes. λ_refracted = λ_air / n = 600 / 1.5 = 400 nm.

sub_questions.text: (ख) 16 cm फोकस दूरी का कोई समतलोत्तल लेंस अपवर्तनांक 1.4 के पदार्थ का बना है। लेंस के वक्रित पृष्ठ की त्रिज्या परिकलित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) A plano-convex lens of focal length 16 cm is made of a material of refractive index 1.4. Calculate the radius of the curved surface of the lens.

key_points: Using lensmaker's equation: 1/f = (n–1)[1/R₁ – 1/R₂]; for plano-convex: R₁ = R, R₂ = ∞

sub_questions.solution: For a plano-convex lens, one surface is flat (R₂ = ∞) and one is convex (R₁ = R). Using the lensmaker's equation: 1/f = (n – 1)[1/R₁ – 1/R₂] = (1.4 – 1)[1/R – 1/∞] = 0.4 × (1/R). Therefore 1/16 = 0.4/R, giving R = 0.4 × 16 = 6.4 cm. The radius of the curved surface of the plano-convex lens is 6.4 cm.

key_points: See sub-questions for part (a) and part (b)

questions.text: विसरण धारा तथा अपवाह धारा में अन्तर बताइए। p-n संधि निर्माण में इनकी भूमिका समझाइए।
questions.text_english: Differentiate between diffusion current and drift current. Explain their role in the formation of p-n junction.

key_points: Diffusion current: due to concentration gradient of charge carriers (holes from p to n, electrons from n to p); no external field needed
Drift current: due to the electric field of the depletion region; minority carriers drift across the junction
At equilibrium in a p-n junction, diffusion current equals drift current and a depletion region is formed

questions.solution: Diffusion current arises due to the concentration gradient of charge carriers — holes diffuse from the p-side to the n-side and electrons diffuse from the n-side to the p-side, without any external electric field. Drift current, on the other hand, arises due to the built-in electric field established across the depletion region; it drives minority carriers (electrons in p-region and holes in n-region) across the junction in a direction opposite to diffusion current. In p-n junction formation, diffusion of charge carriers creates the depletion region and a built-in electric field. At equilibrium, the drift current exactly equals the diffusion current, resulting in zero net current across the junction.

questions.text: पट्टिकाओं के बीच 1 mm पृथकन वाले वायु से भरे किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र की धारिता 20 pF है। इसे 4.0 μC तक आवेशित किया गया है। यदि पट्टिकाओं पर आवेश समान रहता है, तो पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन 5 mm करने के लिए इसकी पट्टिकाओं को खींचने में किया जाने वाला कार्य परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: An air-filled parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 1 mm has a capacitance of 20 pF. It is charged to 4.0 μC. Calculate the amount of work done to pull its plates to a separation of 5 mm. Assume the charge on the plates remains the same.

key_points: Initial energy: U₁ = Q²/(2C₁) = (4×10⁻⁶)²/(2×20×10⁻¹²) = 0.4 J
New capacitance C₂ = C₁ × (d₁/d₂) = 20 × (1/5) = 4 pF
Final energy: U₂ = Q²/(2C₂) = (4×10⁻⁶)²/(2×4×10⁻¹²) = 2.0 J; Work done = U₂ – U₁ = 1.6 J

questions.solution: The initial capacitance is C₁ = 20 pF and initial charge Q = 4.0 μC = 4 × 10⁻⁶ C. Initial energy stored: U₁ = Q²/(2C₁) = (4 × 10⁻⁶)² / (2 × 20 × 10⁻¹²) = 16 × 10⁻¹² / (40 × 10⁻¹²) = 0.4 J. When the plate separation is increased from 1 mm to 5 mm with charge constant, the new capacitance C₂ = C₁ × (d₁/d₂) = 20 × (1/5) = 4 pF. Final energy stored: U₂ = Q²/(2C₂) = (4 × 10⁻⁶)² / (2 × 4 × 10⁻¹²) = 16 × 10⁻¹² / (8 × 10⁻¹²) = 2.0 J. Work done = U₂ – U₁ = 2.0 – 0.4 = 1.6 J.

questions.text: (क) धारा घनत्व परिभाषित कीजिए। क्या यह अदिश या सदिश है? किसी धातु के चालक में कोई विद्युत-क्षेत्र E बनाए रखा गया है। यदि इस चालक में प्रति एकांक आयतन में इलेक्ट्रॉनों (द्रव्यमान m, आवेश e) की संख्या n है तथा इसका विश्रान्ति काल τ है, तो यह दर्शाइए कि धारा घनत्व j = σE है, जहाँ σ = ne²τ/m है।
questions.text_english: (a) Define current density. Is it a scalar or a vector? An electric field E is maintained in a metallic conductor. If n be the number of electrons (mass m, charge e) per unit volume in the conductor and τ its relaxation time, show that the current density j = σE, where σ = ne²τ/m.

sub_questions.text: (क) धारा घनत्व परिभाषित कीजिए। क्या यह अदिश या सदिश है? ... j = σE दर्शाइए।
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Define current density. Is it a scalar or a vector? Show that j = σE where σ = ne²τ/m.

key_points: Current density j = I/A; it is a vector quantity directed along the direction of conventional current
Drift velocity vd = eEτ/m; current density j = nevd = ne(eEτ/m) = (ne²τ/m)E = σE
Thus σ = ne²τ/m (Ohm's law in microscopic form)

sub_questions.solution: Current density is defined as the current flowing per unit cross-sectional area of the conductor, j = I/A. It is a vector quantity, directed along the direction of flow of conventional current (i.e., opposite to the drift of electrons). When an electric field E is applied, electrons acquire a drift velocity vd = eEτ/m, where e is the charge of the electron, m is its mass and τ is the relaxation time. The current density is j = n e vd = ne × (eEτ/m) = (ne²τ/m)E. Comparing with j = σE, we get σ = ne²τ/m, which is Ohm's law in microscopic form.

sub_questions.text: (ख) व्हीटस्टोन सेतु किसे कहते हैं? व्हीटस्टोन सेतु के संतुलन के लिए आवश्यक शर्तें प्राप्त कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) What is a Wheatstone bridge? Obtain the necessary conditions under which the Wheatstone bridge is balanced.

key_points: Wheatstone bridge: circuit with four resistors P, Q, R, S in a diamond arrangement with a galvanometer across one diagonal
Balanced condition: no current through galvanometer; derived using Kirchhoff's laws
Balance condition: P/Q = R/S

sub_questions.solution: A Wheatstone bridge is a circuit consisting of four resistors P, Q, R, and S arranged in a diamond (rhombus) shape, with a battery connected across one diagonal and a galvanometer across the other. When the bridge is balanced, no current flows through the galvanometer. Applying Kirchhoff's laws at the balanced condition: the current through P equals the current through R (let it be I₁), and the current through Q equals the current through S (let it be I₂). The potential at junctions B and D are equal. This gives I₁P = I₂R and I₁Q = I₂S. Dividing: P/Q = R/S. This is the balance condition of the Wheatstone bridge.

key_points: See sub-questions (a) and (b)

questions.solution: This question has two alternatives. See sub-questions (a) and (b) for detailed solutions.
questions.topic: Current density and Ohm's law; Wheatstone bridge

questions.text: अनुप्रस्थ-काट क्षेत्रफल 0.2 cm² की किसी वृत्ताकार कुण्डली से 4 A धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है। इसे 0.5 T परिमाण के एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में इस प्रकार रखा गया है कि कुण्डली का तल चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र के अभिलम्बवत् हो। परिकलित कीजिए : (क) कुण्डली पर नेट बल, (ख) कुण्डली पर बल-आघूर्ण, (ग) इस कुण्डली के प्रत्येक इलेक्ट्रॉन पर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र के कारण औसत बल। इस कुण्डली के पदार्थ में मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व 10²⁸ m⁻³ है।
questions.text_english: A circular coil with cross-sectional area 0.2 cm² carries a current of 4 A. It is kept in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.5 T normal to the plane of the coil. Calculate : (a) the net force on the coil, (b) the torque on the coil, (c) the average force on each electron in the coil due to the magnetic field. The free electron density in the material of the coil is 10²⁸ m⁻³.

key_points: (a) Net force = 0 (uniform field, closed loop)
(b) Torque = 0 (plane of coil is perpendicular to B, so magnetic moment is parallel to B, θ = 0°)

questions.solution: (a) In a uniform magnetic field, the net force on any closed current loop is zero, regardless of its shape. Hence the net force on the coil is zero. (b) The torque on a current loop is τ = NIAB sinθ, where θ is the angle between the magnetic moment and the field. Since the plane of the coil is perpendicular to B, the magnetic moment is parallel to B, so θ = 0° and τ = 0. (c) The drift velocity of electrons is vd = I/(neA) = 4 / (10²⁸ × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 0.2×10⁻⁴) = 4 / (3.2×10⁴) = 1.25×10⁻⁴ m/s. The average magnetic force on each electron is F = evdB = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 1.25×10⁻⁴ × 0.5 = 10⁻²³ N.
questions.topic: Force and torque on a current loop in magnetic field

questions.text: (क) किसी परिपथ में ac स्रोत की आवृत्ति के साथ निम्नलिखित के विचरण को दर्शाने के लिए ग्राफ खींचिए : (i) प्रतिरोध, (ii) संधारित्र प्रतिघात, (iii) प्रेरणिक प्रतिघात। (ख) क्या किसी श्रेणी LCR परिपथ में किसी प्रेरक अथवा संधारित्र के सिरों पर वोल्टता पात ac स्रोत की अनुप्रयुक्त वोल्टता से अधिक हो सकती है? अपने उत्तर की पुष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Draw the graphs showing the variation of the following with the frequency of ac source in a circuit: (i) Resistance, (ii) Capacitive reactance, (iii) Inductive reactance. (b) Can the voltage drop across the inductor or the capacitor in a series LCR circuit be greater than the applied voltage of the ac source? Justify your answer.

key_points: (a) Resistance R is constant with frequency (horizontal line); Capacitive reactance Xc = 1/(2πfC) decreases hyperbolically with frequency; Inductive reactance XL = 2πfL increases linearly with frequency
(b) Yes, the voltage across L or C can exceed the applied voltage in a series LCR circuit
At resonance, VL = VC = IXL, and since the impedance Z is minimum (= R), the current I is maximum, making VL and VC very large compared to applied voltage V

questions.solution: (a) Resistance R does not depend on frequency; its graph is a horizontal straight line. Capacitive reactance Xc = 1/(2πfC) is inversely proportional to frequency; its graph is a hyperbola decreasing with increasing frequency. Inductive reactance XL = 2πfL is directly proportional to frequency; its graph is a straight line through the origin with positive slope. (b) Yes, the voltage across an inductor or capacitor in a series LCR circuit can exceed the applied voltage. This happens near resonance, where the impedance is minimum (Z = R) and current I = V/R is maximum. The voltage across the inductor VL = IXL = (V/R)(2πf₀L) and similarly VC can be very large if XL >> R or Xc >> R, i.e., at high Q factor. This does not violate energy conservation as VL and VC are 180° out of phase and their net contribution to power is zero.

questions.text: (क) नाभिक के किन्हीं दो गुणों को लिखिए। (ख) किसी परमाणु की अपेक्षा नाभिक का घनत्व बहुत अधिक क्यों होता है? (ग) यह दर्शाइए कि सभी नाभिकों के लिए नाभिकीय द्रव्य का घनत्व समान होता है।
questions.text_english: (a) State any two properties of a nucleus. (b) Why is the density of a nucleus much more than that of an atom? (c) Show that the density of the nuclear matter is the same for all nuclei.

key_points: (a) Two properties: (1) Nucleus contains protons and neutrons (nucleons); (2) Nuclear size follows R = R₀A^(1/3) where R₀ ≈ 1.2 fm
(b) The nucleus contains almost all the mass of the atom in an extremely small volume; its radius is ~10⁻¹⁵ m compared to atomic radius ~10⁻¹⁰ m
(c) ρ = M/V = (A × mₙ) / (4/3 π R₀³ A) = 3mₙ/(4πR₀³) = constant, independent of A

questions.solution: (a) Two properties of a nucleus: (1) A nucleus consists of protons and neutrons, collectively called nucleons. The number of protons equals the atomic number Z and the total number of nucleons equals the mass number A. (2) The radius of a nucleus follows the empirical relation R = R₀A^(1/3), where R₀ ≈ 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, showing that the volume of the nucleus is proportional to A. (b) A nucleus has a very small radius (~10⁻¹⁵ m) but contains nearly all the mass of the atom. The atomic radius is much larger (~10⁻¹⁰ m), so most of the atom is empty space. Therefore, the density of the nucleus is many orders of magnitude greater than that of the atom. (c) Nuclear density ρ = mass/volume = (A × mₙ) / (4/3 π R³) = (A mₙ) / (4/3 π R₀³ A) = 3mₙ/(4πR₀³). Since mₙ and R₀ are constants, ρ is independent of A, proving that nuclear density is the same for all nuclei.

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर के सिद्धांत के तीन अभिगृहीतों का उल्लेख कीजिए। कोई हाइड्रोजन परमाणु स्तर n से स्तर (n–1) को व्युत्तेजित होता है। यह दर्शाइए कि बोर के सिद्धांत के अनुसार, n के बृहत् मानों के लिए उत्सर्जित विकिरणों की आवृत्ति v ∝ n⁻³ होती है, जहाँ यह ठीक-ठीक मेल खाता है और यह बोर के सिद्धांत की सफलताओं में से एक है।
questions.text_english: State the three postulates of Bohr's theory for hydrogen atom. A hydrogen atom de-excites from level n to level (n–1). Show that, for large values of n, the frequency v of the emitted radiation is proportional to n⁻³, which exactly agrees with classical physics. This result is one of the successes of Bohr's theory.

key_points: Three postulates: (1) Electrons move in discrete circular orbits; (2) Angular momentum is quantized: L = nh/(2π); (3) Energy is radiated only during transition between orbits
Energy of level n: Eₙ = –13.6/n² eV; energy emitted = Eₙ – Eₙ₋₁
For large n: ΔE ≈ 13.6 × 2/n³ eV; v = ΔE/h ∝ 1/n³ = n⁻³

questions.solution: The three postulates of Bohr's theory: (1) Electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits around the nucleus without radiating energy. (2) Only those orbits are allowed in which the angular momentum of the electron is an integral multiple of h/(2π), i.e., L = nh/(2π). (3) Energy is emitted or absorbed only when an electron transitions between two allowed orbits, with the frequency of radiation given by hν = E_initial – E_final. For the transition from level n to (n–1): the energy difference ΔE = Eₙ₋₁ – Eₙ = 13.6[1/(n–1)² – 1/n²] eV. For large n, (n–1) ≈ n, so 1/(n–1)² – 1/n² ≈ 2/n³. Therefore ΔE ≈ 13.6 × 2/n³ eV. The frequency of emitted radiation ν = ΔE/h ∝ 1/n³, i.e., ν ∝ n⁻³. This is consistent with the classical result that a charged particle in a circular orbit of radius proportional to n² has orbital frequency proportional to n⁻³.

questions.text: (क) विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंग की तरंगदैर्घ्य को प्रायः विकिरण उत्पन्न करने वाले निकाय के अभिलाक्षणिक साइज़ से संबंधित किया जाता है। इस कथन की पुष्टि के लिए दो उदाहरण दीजिए। (ख) (i) लम्बी दूरियों के रेडियो प्रसारण के लिए लघु-तरंग बैण्ड का उपयोग किया जाता है। क्यों? questions.text_english: (a) The wavelength of electromagnetic waves is often related to the characteristic size of the system producing the radiation. Give two examples to justify this statement. (b) (i) Long distance radio broadcasts use short-wave bands. Why? (ii) Optical and radio telescopes are built on the ground, but X-ray astronomy is possible only from satellites orbiting the Earth. Why?

key_points: (a) Example 1: Radio waves have wavelengths of metres, produced by oscillating currents in antennas of comparable size. Example 2: X-rays have wavelengths ~0.1 nm, similar to atomic size; produced by electron transitions in inner atomic shells
(b)(i) Short waves are reflected by the ionosphere and can travel long distances by multiple reflections
(b)(ii) Earth's atmosphere absorbs X-rays; X-ray astronomy requires space-based satellites above the atmosphere

questions.solution: (a) Example 1: Radio waves have wavelengths of the order of metres to kilometres, and they are generated by oscillating electrons in antennas of comparable size. Example 2: Visible light has wavelengths of around 400–700 nm, which is comparable to atomic dimensions; it is emitted when electrons in atoms transition between outer energy levels, which are of atomic-scale dimensions. (b)(i) Short-wave bands (wavelengths 10–100 m) are reflected by the ionosphere and can travel around the Earth by successive reflections between the ionosphere and the Earth's surface. This makes them ideal for long-distance communication. (ii) The Earth's atmosphere is opaque to X-rays — they are absorbed by oxygen, nitrogen, and other atmospheric gases. Hence, X-ray astronomy cannot be done from the ground. Satellites orbiting above the atmosphere have a clear path for X-ray detection. Optical and radio waves, however, can pass through the atmosphere, so ground-based telescopes work for these.

The power of a lens is reciprocal of its focal length. If a number of lenses are kept in contact, the power of the combination is the algebraic sum of the powers of the individual lenses.

sub_questions.solution: Using lensmaker's formula: 1/f = (n–1)[1/R₁ – 1/R₂]. For a double-convex lens with both radii equal to R: R₁ = +R and R₂ = –R. So 1/f = (n–1)[1/R – (–1/R)] = (n–1)(2/R). Power P = 1/f = 2(n–1)/R. Option A is correct.

sub_questions.solution: When a double-convex lens is cut perpendicular to its principal axis into two equal halves, each half is a plano-convex lens. For each half, one surface has radius of curvature R (convex) and the other is flat (R = ∞). Using lensmaker's formula: 1/f' = (n–1)[1/R – 0] = (n–1)/R. But the original lens had power P = 2(n–1)/R. questions.text: संधि डायोड दिष्टकारी के रूप में : ac वोल्टता को दिष्ट (dc) वोल्टता में परिवर्तित करने की प्रक्रिया को दिष्टकरण कहते हैं और इस परिवर्तन को सम्पन्न करने वाली युक्ति को दिष्टकारी कहते हैं। किसी p-n संधि डायोड के अभिलाक्षणिकों से यह ज्ञात होता है कि जब p-n संधि डायोड अग्रदिशिक बायसित होता है, तो उसका प्रतिरोध निम्न होता है तथा जब पश्चदिशिक बायसित होता है, तो उसका प्रतिरोध उच्च होता है। अतः p-n संधि डायोड केवल अग्रदिशिक बायस होने पर ही चालन करता है। p-n संधि डायोड का यही गुण दिष्टकारी के रूप में इसके उपयोग के लिए इसे उपयुक्त बनाता है। इस प्रकार, जब किसी ac वोल्टता को किसी p-n संधि के सिरों पर अनुप्रयुक्त किया जाता है, तो यह केवल उन्हीं प्रत्यावर्ती अर्ध-चक्रों में चालन करती है जब यह अग्रदिशिक बायस होती है। वह दिष्टकारी जो किसी ac वोल्टता के अर्ध-चक्र का दिष्टकरण करता है, उसे अर्ध-तरंग दिष्टकारी कहते हैं और जो दोनों अर्ध-चक्रों का दिष्टकरण करता है, उसे पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी कहते हैं।
questions.text_english: Junction Diode as a Rectifier: The process of conversion of an ac voltage into a dc voltage is called rectification and the device which performs this conversion is called a rectifier. The characteristics of a p-n junction diode reveal that when a p-n junction diode is forward biased, it offers a low resistance and when it is reverse biased, it offers a high resistance. Hence, a p-n junction diode conducts only when it is forward biased. This property of a p-n junction diode makes it suitable for its use as a rectifier. Thus, when an ac voltage is applied across a p-n junction, it conducts only during those alternate half cycles for which it is forward biased. A rectifier which rectifies only half cycle of an ac voltage is called a half-wave rectifier and one that rectifies both the half cycles is known as a full-wave rectifier.

sub_questions.text: किसी पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी पर अनुप्रयुक्त किसी प्रत्यावर्ती वोल्टता का वर्ग माध्य मूल मान V₀/√2 है। तो दिष्टीकृत निर्गत वोल्टता का वर्ग माध्य मूल मान है :
sub_questions.text_english: The root mean square value of an alternating voltage applied to a full-wave rectifier is V₀/√2. Then the root mean square value of the rectified output voltage is :
sub_questions.solution: For a full-wave rectifier, both half cycles are rectified. The output is a full-wave rectified waveform. For a sinusoidal input v = V₀ sinωt, the rms value of the input is V₀/√2. The rms value of the output of a full-wave rectifier is the same as that of the input sine wave, which is V₀/√2. This is because rectification does not change the rms value — it only makes all the half cycles positive. Therefore the answer is (A) V₀/√2.

options_english.B: Half cycle of the input signal

sub_questions.solution: In a full-wave rectifier (using two diodes in a centre-tap configuration or four diodes in a bridge), each diode conducts only during half a cycle of the input signal. During the first half cycle, one diode is forward biased and conducts; during the second half cycle, the other diode is forward biased and conducts. So each individual diode carries current for only half the cycle. The output is a full-wave rectified signal because the two diodes alternate. Option B is correct.

questions.text_english: (a) (i) A resistor and a capacitor are connected in series to an ac source v = vₘ sin ωt. Derive an expression for the impedance of the circuit. (ii) When does an inductor act as a conductor in a circuit? Give reason for it. (iii) An electric lamp is designed to operate at 110 V dc and 11 A current. If the lamp is operated on 220 V, 50 Hz ac source with a coil in series, then find the inductance of the coil.

key_points: (i) Impedance Z = √(R² + Xc²) = √(R² + 1/(ω²C²))
(ii) Inductor acts as conductor at very high frequency (XL = ωL → ∞ blocks current) — actually at DC or very low frequency (ω→0, XL→0, acts as short circuit/conductor)
(iii) Lamp resistance R = V/I = 110/11 = 10 Ω; required impedance Z = 220/11 = 20 Ω; XL = √(Z²–R²) = √(400–100) = √300; L = XL/ω = √300/(2π×50)

sub_questions.solution: (i) In a series RC circuit with ac source v = vₘ sin ωt, the voltage across R is VR = IR (in phase with current) and across C is VC = IXC (lagging current by 90°). The total voltage phasor: V² = VR² + VC² = I²R² + I²Xc². Therefore the impedance Z = V/I = √(R² + Xc²) = √(R² + 1/(ω²C²)). The phase angle φ = arctan(Xc/R). (ii) An inductor acts as a conductor (pure resistor with negligible reactance) at very low frequencies or for DC. Since XL = ωL, when ω → 0 (DC), XL → 0 and the inductor offers no opposition, behaving like a simple conductor. This is because a DC current creates a constant magnetic field, producing no back-EMF and hence no opposition. (iii) Lamp resistance R = V/I = 110/11 = 10 Ω. When connected to 220 V ac, the same current 11 A must flow. Required impedance Z = Vrms/I = 220/11 = 20 Ω. Inductive reactance XL = √(Z² – R²) = √(400 – 100) = √300 = 10√3 Ω. Inductance L = XL/(2πf) = 10√3/(2π × 50) = √3/(10π) ≈ 0.055 H.

sub_questions.text_english: (b) (i) Draw a labelled diagram of a step-up transformer and describe its working principle. Explain any three causes for energy losses in a real transformer. (ii) A step-up transformer converts a low voltage into high voltage. Does it violate the principle of conservation of energy? Explain. (iii) A step-up transformer has 200 and 3000 turns in its primary and secondary coils respectively. The input voltage given to the primary coil is 90 V. Calculate: (1) The output voltage across the secondary coil, (2) The current in the primary coil if the current in the secondary coil is 2.0 A.

key_points: (i) Transformer works on mutual induction; step-up has Ns > Np; energy losses: eddy currents, hysteresis, copper loss (I²R), flux leakage
(ii) No violation — voltage increases but current decreases proportionally; power = VI remains conserved

sub_questions.solution: (b)(i) A step-up transformer consists of a soft iron core with a primary coil (Np turns) and a secondary coil (Ns turns, Ns > Np). When ac voltage is applied to the primary, it creates a changing magnetic flux in the core, which induces an EMF in the secondary coil according to Faraday's law. The ratio Vs/Vp = Ns/Np > 1, so secondary voltage exceeds primary voltage. Three energy losses: (1) Eddy current losses — induced currents in the iron core dissipate energy as heat; minimised by laminating the core. (2) Hysteresis losses — energy is dissipated in repeatedly magnetising and demagnetising the core; minimised by using soft iron. (3) Copper losses — heat produced in the resistance of primary and secondary windings (I²R); minimised by using thick copper wires. (ii) A step-up transformer does not violate energy conservation. Although it increases voltage, the current in the secondary is proportionally reduced so that Vp × Ip ≈ Vs × Is. The power output cannot exceed the power input; in an ideal transformer they are equal. (iii)(1) Vs = Vp × (Ns/Np) = 90 × (3000/200) = 90 × 15 = 1350 V. (2) For an ideal transformer, VpIp = VsIs, so Ip = Is × Ns/Np = 2.0 × (3000/200) = 2.0 × 15 = 30 A.

questions.text: (क) (i) किसी बाह्य एकसमान विद्युत-क्षेत्र E में किसी विद्युत द्विध्रुव p की स्थितिज ऊर्जा के लिए कोई व्यंजक व्युत्पन्न कीजिए। इस द्विध्रुव की स्थितिज ऊर्जा कब (1) अधिकतम, और (2) न्यूनतम होती है? (ii) कोई विद्युत द्विध्रुव बिन्दु आवेश –1.0 pC और +1.0 pC जो xy तल में क्रमश: (0,0) और (3 mm, 4 mm) पर स्थित हैं, से मिलकर बना है। इस प्रदेश में किसी विद्युत-क्षेत्र E = (1000 V/m) î को लगाया गया है। द्विध्रुव पर कार्यरत बल-आघूर्ण ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) (i) Derive an expression for potential energy of an electric dipole p in an external uniform electric field E. When is the potential energy of the dipole (1) maximum, and (2) minimum? (ii) An electric dipole consists of point charges –1.0 pC and +1.0 pC located at (0,0) and (3 mm, 4 mm) respectively in x-y plane. An electric field E = (1000 V/m) î is switched on in the region. Find the torque acting on the dipole.

key_points: (i) U = –pE cosθ = –p·E; maximum at θ = 180° (U = +pE); minimum at θ = 0° (U = –pE)
(ii) Dipole vector from –q to +q: d = (3mm, 4mm); p = q×d = 1×10⁻¹² × 5×10⁻³ = 5×10⁻¹⁵ C·m
Torque τ = p × E; |τ| = pE sinθ where sinθ = (py/p) = 4/5; τ = 5×10⁻¹⁵ × 1000 × 4/5 = 4×10⁻¹² N·m

sub_questions.solution: (i) When a dipole of moment p is placed in a uniform electric field E at an angle θ, the torque on it is τ = pE sinθ. The work done in rotating the dipole from angle θ₀ to θ is W = pE(cosθ₀ – cosθ). Taking θ₀ = 90° as the reference position (U = 0), the potential energy is U = –pE cosθ = –p·E. The potential energy is (1) maximum when θ = 180°, giving U = +pE (dipole antiparallel to field — unstable equilibrium); and (2) minimum when θ = 0°, giving U = –pE (dipole parallel to field — stable equilibrium). (ii) The dipole vector points from –q to +q, so d = (3–0, 4–0) mm = (3î + 4ĵ) × 10⁻³ m. Dipole moment p = q × d = 1×10⁻¹² × (3î + 4ĵ)×10⁻³ = (3î + 4ĵ) × 10⁻¹⁵ C·m. Electric field E = 1000î V/m. Torque τ = p × E = (3î + 4ĵ) × 10⁻¹⁵ × 1000î = 10⁻¹² [(3î × î) + (4ĵ × î)] = 10⁻¹² [0 + 4(–k̂)] = –4×10⁻¹² k̂ N·m. The magnitude of torque is 4×10⁻¹² N·m directed along –z direction.

sub_questions.text: (ख) (i) 2a दूरी के पृथकन और q तथा –q आवेशों से बना, कोई विद्युत द्विध्रुव (द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण p = p î) x-अक्ष के अनुदिश अपने केन्द्र को मूल-बिन्दु पर रखते हुए स्थित है। यह दर्शाइए कि इस द्विध्रुव के कारण किसी बिन्दु x, (x >> a) पर विभव V = (1/4πε₀) · (p·î)/x² है। (ii) क्रमश: त्रिज्या 1 cm और 3 cm के दो वियुक्त धात्विक गोलों S₁ तथा S₂ को इस प्रकार आवेशित किया गया है कि उनके आवेश घनत्व समान 9×10⁻² C/m² हैं। इन दोनों गोलों को एक-दूसरे से अत्यधिक दूरी पर रखकर किसी पतले तार से संयोजित किया गया है। गोले S₁ पर नया आवेश परिकलित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) (i) An electric dipole (dipole moment p = p î), consisting of charges q and –q, separated by distance 2a, is placed along the x-axis, with its centre at the origin. Show that the potential V, due to this dipole, at a point x, (x >> a) is equal to (1/4πε₀)·(p·î)/x². (ii) Two isolated metallic spheres S₁ and S₂ of radii 1 cm and 3 cm respectively are charged such that both have the same charge density 9×10⁻² C/m². They are placed far away from each other and connected by a thin wire. Calculate the new charge on sphere S₁.

key_points: (i) V = (1/4πε₀)[q/(x–a) – q/(x+a)] = (1/4πε₀)[2qa/(x²–a²)] ≈ (1/4πε₀)(p/x²) for x >> a
(ii) Initial charges: Q₁ = σ×4πr₁² = 9×10⁻²×4π×(10⁻²)² = 36π×10⁻⁶ C; Q₂ = σ×4πr₂² = 9×10⁻²×4π×(3×10⁻²)² = 324π×10⁻⁶ C; Total Q = 360π×10⁻⁶ C
After connection, V₁ = V₂ → Q₁'/r₁ = Q₂'/r₂ → Q₁'/1 = Q₂'/3; Q₁' + Q₂' = Q; Q₁' = Q/4 = 90π×10⁻⁶ ≈ 2.83×10⁻⁴ C

sub_questions.solution: (b)(i) The dipole has +q at x = +a and –q at x = –a. The potential at point P on the x-axis at distance x (x >> a) from the origin is: V = (1/4πε₀)[q/(x–a) + (–q)/(x+a)] = (q/4πε₀)[(x+a–x+a)/((x–a)(x+a))] = (q/4πε₀)[2a/(x²–a²)]. For x >> a, x²–a² ≈ x², so V = (1/4πε₀)(2qa/x²) = (1/4πε₀)(p/x²), since p = 2qa = dipole moment. This proves V = (p·î/x²)/(4πε₀). (ii) Initial charge on S₁: Q₁ = σ × 4πr₁² = 9×10⁻² × 4π × (0.01)² = 36π × 10⁻⁶ C. Initial charge on S₂: Q₂ = σ × 4πr₂² = 9×10⁻² × 4π × (0.03)² = 324π × 10⁻⁶ C. Total charge Q = Q₁ + Q₂ = 360π × 10⁻⁶ C. After connecting by wire, both reach the same potential: Q₁'/r₁ = Q₂'/r₂, so Q₁'/1 = Q₂'/3, giving Q₂' = 3Q₁'. Also Q₁' + Q₂' = 360π×10⁻⁶, so 4Q₁' = 360π×10⁻⁶, thus Q₁' = 90π×10⁻⁶ ≈ 2.83×10⁻⁴ C.

questions.text: (क) (i) कोई प्रकाश किरण किसी त्रिभुजाकार प्रिज़्म से गुज़रती है। आपतन कोण के साथ विचलन कोण किस प्रकार विचरण करता है? ग्राफ द्वारा दर्शाइए। अतः न्यूनतम विचलन कोण परिभाषित कीजिए। (ii) कोई प्रकाश किरण प्रिज़्म कोण A के किसी प्रिज़्म के एक अपवर्तक फलक पर अभिलम्बवत् आपतन करके कोण δ पर विचलित होती है। सिद्ध कीजिए कि प्रिज़्म के पदार्थ का अपवर्तनांक n = sin(A+δ)/sin A है। (iii) किसी प्रिज़्म के पदार्थ का अपवर्तनांक √2 है। यदि प्रिज़्म का अपवर्तक कोण 60° है, तो ज्ञात कीजिए : (1) न्यूनतम विचलन कोण, तथा (2) आपतन कोण।
questions.text_english: (a) (i) A ray of light passes through a triangular prism. Show graphically, how the angle of deviation varies with the angle of incidence? Hence define the angle of minimum deviation. (ii) A ray of light is incident normally on a refracting face of a prism of prism angle A and suffers a deviation of angle δ. Prove that the refractive index n of the material of the prism is given by n = sin(A+δ)/sin A. (iii) The refractive index of the material of a prism is √2. If the refracting angle of the prism is 60°, find the: (1) Angle of minimum deviation, and (2) Angle of incidence.

key_points: (i) Graph: deviation δ vs angle of incidence i has a minimum at some angle; minimum deviation δₘ is defined as the minimum value of δ
(ii) Normal incidence on first face means r₁ = 0°; r₂ = A; Snell's law at second face: n sin A = sin(A+δ); hence n = sin(A+δ)/sin A
(iii) n = √2, A = 60°; at minimum deviation: n = sin((A+δₘ)/2)/sin(A/2); √2 = sin((60+δₘ)/2)/sin30°; sin((60+δₘ)/2) = √2×0.5 = 1/√2; (60+δₘ)/2 = 45°; δₘ = 30°; angle of incidence = (A+δₘ)/2 = 45°

sub_questions.solution: (i) When a ray of light passes through a prism, the angle of deviation δ decreases as the angle of incidence i increases from 0°, reaches a minimum value δₘ at a particular angle, and then increases again. The graph is a U-shaped curve with a minimum. The angle of minimum deviation δₘ is defined as the minimum value of the angle of deviation experienced by a light ray passing through the prism, which occurs when the ray passes symmetrically through the prism (i.e., the refracted ray inside the prism is parallel to the base). (ii) When a ray is incident normally on the first face, the angle of refraction at the first face r₁ = 0°. For a prism of angle A, r₁ + r₂ = A, so r₂ = A. The ray exits the second face at angle (A + δ) to the normal of the first face — i.e., the angle of emergence e = A + δ. Applying Snell's law at the second face: n sin A = 1 × sin(A + δ), hence n = sin(A + δ)/sin A. (iii) n = √2, A = 60°. Using the minimum deviation formula: n = sin((A + δₘ)/2) / sin(A/2). So √2 = sin((60° + δₘ)/2) / sin 30° = sin((60° + δₘ)/2) / 0.5. Therefore sin((60° + δₘ)/2) = √2/2 = 1/√2, giving (60° + δₘ)/2 = 45°, so 60° + δₘ = 90°, hence δₘ = 30°. The angle of incidence at minimum deviation: i = (A + δₘ)/2 = (60° + 30°)/2 = 45°.

sub_questions.text: (ख) (i) हाइगेन्स का सिद्धांत लिखिए। कोई समतल तरंग किसी परावर्ती पृष्ठ पर कोण i पर आपतन करती है। तदनुरूपी परावर्तित तरंगाग्र की रचना कीजिए। इस आरेख का उपयोग करके, सिद्ध कीजिए कि परावर्तन कोण आपतन कोण के बराबर होता है। (ii) प्रकाश के कला-संबद्ध स्रोत क्या होते हैं? क्या दो स्वतंत्र सोडियम लैम्प कला-संबद्ध स्रोतों के रूप में कार्य कर सकते हैं? व्याख्या कीजिए। (iii) यंग के द्विपरी प्रयोग में किसी प्रकाश पुंज द्वारा, जिसमें दो तरंगदैर्घ्य, एक ज्ञात तरंगदैर्घ्य λ₁ = 520 nm की तथा दूसरी अज्ञात तरंगदैर्घ्य λ की है, दो ऐसे व्यतिकरण पैटर्न उत्पन्न करते हैं, जिनमें अज्ञात तरंगदैर्घ्य की चतुर्थ दीप्त फ्रिंज ज्ञात तरंगदैर्घ्य की पंचम दीप्त फ्रिंज के संपाती है। λ का मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) (i) State Huygens principle. A plane wave is incident at an angle i on a reflecting surface. Construct the corresponding reflected wavefront. Using this diagram, prove that the angle of reflection is equal to the angle of incidence. (ii) What are the coherent sources of light? Can two independent sodium lamps act like coherent sources? Explain. (iii) A beam of light consisting of a known wavelength λ₁ = 520 nm and an unknown wavelength λ in Young's double slit experiment produces two interference patterns such that the fourth bright fringe of unknown wavelength coincides with the fifth bright fringe of known wavelength. Find the value of λ.

key_points: (i) Huygens: every point on a wavefront is a source of secondary wavelets; law of reflection proved using geometry of wavefront construction
(ii) Coherent sources: same frequency and constant phase difference; two independent sodium lamps cannot be coherent as they emit independently with random phase changes

sub_questions.solution: (b)(i) Huygens' Principle states that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets that spread out with the speed of light in that medium, and the new wavefront at any later time is the common tangent (envelope) to all these secondary wavelets. For a plane wave incident at angle i on a reflecting surface: the wavefront AC is drawn, and from point A secondary wavelets are constructed. While the wavelet from A travels a distance equal to BC (which the incident ray covers), the reflected wavefront BD is drawn tangent to the secondary wavelet from A. Using triangles ABC and ABD: BC = AD (same time), AB is common, angle ABC = angle ABD = 90°. Hence triangles are congruent, so angle i = angle r (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection). (ii) Coherent sources are those that have the same frequency and a constant (or zero) phase difference between them. Two independent sodium lamps cannot act as coherent sources because each lamp emits light due to random atomic transitions. The phase differences between emissions from different atoms change randomly and very rapidly, so no stable interference pattern can be formed. Coherent sources are typically produced by splitting light from a single source. (iii) In Young's double slit experiment, the position of the nth bright fringe for wavelength λ is yₙ = nλD/d. For the fourth bright fringe of λ to coincide with the fifth bright fringe of λ₁: 4λD/d = 5λ₁D/d. Therefore 4λ = 5 × 520 nm, giving λ = 5 × 520/4 = 650 nm.
